evidence.claim: The bank's model scored this transaction 0.76, in its second-highest band.
The purchase was made online, without the card present.
The amount is $35.66, under the $500 band.
The amount is $35.66, not the sub-$5 size a probe authorisation uses.
Every one of the card's unnamed match flags (M1-M9) is true.
The transaction carries no distance value (an unnamed Vesta field).
The identity record marks this device as new for the account.
The identity record does not carry the 'Found' device state.
No proxy was recorded on the connection.
This card has never been used on this device before.
The card has 1 prior purchases of product code C.
The previous transaction on this card was 35 minutes earlier.
The previous transaction was more than ten minutes earlier.
35 prior charges on this card fall within $0.50 of $35.66.
$35.66 is below this card's own prior mean of $114.31.
$35.66 is within two standard deviations of this card's prior mean ($543.18).
A step-up authentication challenge went uncompleted on an unrecognised device.

Fraud Policy §3a. A case is not a report — applied here because 3a: no report. exposure $35.66 is at or below $1,000; the activity connects to no shared device profile, region cluster or other customer's fraud.

case.summary: The evidence shows an online card-not-present purchase on a device marked new for this account, with every one of the unnamed match flags true and no proxy recorded. That combination is consistent with card-not-present fraud from a new device, but it is not proof by itself because the amount is $35.66 and there are legitimate-looking features such as prior activity at similar amounts and a 35 minute gap from the previous transaction. The history also includes prior confirmed fraud on this card and prior cleared alerts where the cardholder said a new phone was theirs, so the device signal is important but not decisive on its own.
